the other incorrectly relates ages from different times.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01561","case1_error":"Reduces the required rope length by 25% instead of accounting for reduced usable length of purchased rope.","case2_error":"Uses Rudy’s 10 mph speed for Grayson’s second leg instead of the specified 20 mph.","reason":"One applies a loss adjustment incorrectly; the other substitutes another traveler’s speed.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01562","case1_error":"Subtracts leaking fill time from normal fill time, producing the wrong sign for the requested additional time.","case2_error":"Charges all 500 flowers as roses and again as lilies, rather than pricing each flower type’s actual count.","reason":"The first reverses subtraction in its derivation; the second double-counts mixed categories when calculating costs.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01563","case1_error":"Incorrectly changes O = 0.25T to O = 0.25(T − 72), then claims O = 2 from O = 0.25O.","case2_error":"Reports the original total, including the 100 eaten yellow candies, instead of the remaining candies.","reason":"The first contains invalid algebraic transformations; the second computes the wrong requested quantity despite correct initial counts.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01564","case1_error":"Computes Jack’s current apples divided by Jack’s capacity, instead of Jill’s capacity divided by Jack’s current apples.","case2_error":"Uses cumulative distances across months to establish marathon readiness instead of the distance achievable in a single month.","reason":"The first constructs the wrong capacity ratio; the second substitutes accumulated training distance for running capability.","judgment":"different"}]}
